newsitem.title: THAILAND: Central bankers meeting overshadowed by Thai woes.
newsitem.headline: Central bankers meeting overshadowed by Thai woes.

text.p: The end of the 32nd meeting of the Southeast Asian Central Bank Governors (SEACEN) was overshadowed on Friday by the problems of its host nation, Thailand.
The meeting began on Thursday and after a brief opening ceremony -- at which Thai central bank governor Rerngchai Marakanond spoke -- was closed to the media.
Thursday saw the Thai stock market index plunge by some 3.4 percent to end at a 56-month low of 698.06.

One of the reasons for the fall was negative market reaction to some of Rerngchai's remarks at the opening ceremony about central bank efforts to strengthen finance companies, which have been facing short-term liquidity problems.
The local Thai language media blamed the stock market malaise on Rerngchai.
On Friday, Moody's Investors Service said it may downgrade ratings on Thailand's long-term debt, a move analysts said could heap even more pressure on the weak stock market and baht.
Moody's said the review of Thailand's present A2 rating was prompted by concerns regarding the soundness of Thailand's financial sector as well as constraints on macro-economic policy-making.
The stock market took a dim view of this, and at one stage plummetted by more than four percent.
Responding to the news of the potential downgrading, dozens of Thai reporters descended upon the plush five-star hotel where the SEACEN gathering was taking place.
As the central bankers broke for lunch, security officials became concerned at the number of journalists gathered and smuggled Rerngchai from the hotel.
Two local journalists who saw him as he climbed into a car said he waved his arms at them and shouted, "This is not the time, this is not the time."

Rerngchai was successfully returned to the meeting after lunch and at the end of the day again managed a disappearing act to the chagrin of the reporters who had wanted to ask him about Thailand's problems.
The annual SEACEN gatherings are not on a par with Group of Seven (G7) meetings, where decisions on monetry policies can rock world financial markets.
In the words of one governor, it is merely an annual gathering amongst friends to discuss their respctive successes and failures without intrusion from the press.
The SEACEN meeting itself did not produce any fireworks.
A communique issued at the end of the day was essentially a reprise of remarks at the opening ceremony.
But the Thai stock market had the last word. In the last hour of trading it rallied sharply to end over two percent higher as Far Eastern investors were tempted to buy at the low levels.
